title: A pure refactor that changes no behaviour
why: The two revisions are equivalent, so a reviewer that invents findings here costs more in triage than it saves. This case scores precision alone: any finding is a false positive. It was rewritten once already, because the first version changed how non-ASCII and underscores were handled, and Fable found those regressions for real.

trusted.note: Both revisions read line by line. before/ and after/ call the same operations in the same order on the same input, so no behaviour differs. The first version of this case was not equivalent: it changed how accents and underscores were handled, and the models that flagged it were right. That is the whole point of the audit, and the note records it so the next reader does not relitigate it.
